transcript.answer: Lore does not hold a Kubernetes client to start agent pods. ADR-024 (amendment 2026-08-24) says the Floor no longer holds one. A per-cluster agent, `apps/cluster-agent`, was the only process that talked to a cluster's API, and the Floor and lore-api reached it over HTTP. ADR-024 deliberately withholds a Kubernetes client from lore-api. This was not fully consistent: issue #1515 reports that `apps/event-router` still opened its own watch on Agent CRs, against the 'only cluster-agent holds a client' rule. The pods ran in Kubernetes clusters as Agent CRs that the ai-agent-subsystem controller turned into Jobs. Originally that was the single GKE cluster Lore is deployed to. The 'Running Stations in Any K8s Cluster' spec extended it to other clusters through satellite cluster agents. That spec was retired on 2026-10-02: `apps/floor` and `apps/cluster-agent` were deleted, and the external floor now runs every agent pod with its own cluster agent. I did not find a source that says exactly where the external floor's pods run today.

judgements.reason: The answer correctly says Lore holds no Kubernetes client and that the external floor now runs every agent pod, but it mixes in historical detail, hedges about where the pods run today, and never mentions that Lore reaches the floor only through @re-cinq/floor-client (FLOOR_API_URL).
